Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

state noun

condition

also condition, state of things, status (of a thing), current status, in good condition, in bad condition, in excellent condition

classical

Cic. Verr. 1.12: restituī in antīquum statum (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fam. 3.11.4: reī pūblicae statum (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 295

status, statūs m.

noun, fourth declension

condition, state, situation

Other words

  • quō locō rēs est? — what state are things in?

    phrase: locus in the ablative · also used · classical · Liv. 2.47.5: quō locō rēs essent (Lewis & Short); Hor. Ep. 1.12.25: quō sit Rōmāna locō rēs (Lewis & Short)

    In aliquō locō esse, to be in a certain position or state (Lewis & Short s.v. locus); Cicero has the genitive, eōdem locī.

  • bene (male) habitus — in good (bad) condition, well (badly) nourished

    also used · classical · Masurius Sabinus in Gell. 4.20.11: male habitum … habitissimum (Lewis & Short s.v. habeō); Traupman 95; Traupman 295

    Of the body, a man’s or an animal’s; the superlative habitissimus, in excellent condition.

Examples

  • rēs eōdem est locī quō relīquistī

    things are in the same state as you left themCic. Att. 1.13.5

  • Siciliam ita vexāvit ac perdidit ut ea restituī in antīquum statum nūllō modō possit

    he so harried and ruined Sicily that it can never be put back in its former stateCic. Verr. 1.12

  • habitissimus

    in excellent conditionTraupman 295

See also state, situation, condition.
